summary: ```markdown # CLO Skills Workshop - Custom Fabric Sample Materials ## Introduction Welcome to the CLO Skills Workshop! Today, I will explain how to make a zip-up puller. In the previous tutorial video, we focused on the creation of the zip-up puller as an accessory for clothing. With our new version, defining the zip-up puller can achieve a more realistic pull effect. ## Creating a Zip-Up Puller To start, let's create a zip-up puller similar to the reference picture provided in your materials. ### Step 1: Open CLO - Open CLO software. - Locate the zip-up tool in the 2D window. ### Step 2: Set Default Size - Use the default size of **500mm x 500mm**. - Click **OK**. ### Step 3: Add Reference Picture - Add the reference picture of the zip-up puller as a sticker. - Click **OK** to confirm. ### Step 4: Adjust Transparency - Adjust the transparency of the sticker slightly to facilitate drawing the outline and inner line. ### Step 5: Draw the Outline - Use the inner line tool to draw the outline of the zip-up puller. - Note that the thickness of the zip-up puller differs from the main body, so make the zip-up puller thinner. ### Step 6: Create Multi-Sided Line - Use the multi-sided line tool to draw the outline. - Press **CTRL** to assist in designing the curve. - Choose the line geometry for the zip-up puller. ### Step 7: Adjust Curve Points - Draw the curve inside the puller. - Adjust the position of the curve points with a ruler. - Make minor adjustments to improve the overall shape. ### Step 8: Finalize the Outline - Select the outline and cut it off using the right-click option. ### Step 9: Pattern Adjustment - Since the particle diameter is currently set to 20, the drawn pattern will be a triangular grid. - Adjust the example of this pattern to 1. ## Main Body Drawing ### Step 10: Draw the Main Body - Use the internal multidirectional line tool to draw the main body. - Press the **Shift** key to create a smooth trajectory. ### Step 11: Close the Pattern - Adjust the inner outline and delete unnecessary lines. ### Step 12: Create Holes - Convert the outline lines into holes, including the pull ring. - Delete all stickers that are not needed. ### Step 13: Final Adjustments - Adjust the rendering thickness of the main body to **4mm**. - Adjust the curve of the pull ring to **1mm** and set its curve to **25%**. ## Exporting the Puller ### Step 14: Export OBJ - Select all templates and right-click in the 3D window. - Choose to move to the ground center using the positioning tool. Ensure the ground line passes through the middle of the puller. - Go to **File** > **Export** and select **OBJ**. - Name it **puller1** and click **Save**. ### Step 15: Pre-Select Elements - Ensure all templates, stickers, and accessories are selected before saving. ### Step 16: Importing into Project - Open the project file that needs the puller. - Unzip the compression bag to find the OBJ file. - In the top menu bar, find **Material** and select **Puller**. - Click on the button beside the OBJ file to import the newly created puller. ## Final Adjustments ### Step 17: Resizing the Puller - Adjust the size proportion of the puller to **40%**. - Confirm the adjustments and modify the slanting angle and material type. ### Conclusion This concludes the tutorial on creating a custom zip-up puller along with a three-dimensional metal carving logo effect. You can further adjust the length and width of the puller as needed. Feel free to reach out for any questions or further clarifications! ```
